Empresa.title: Empresa
Empresa.description: Represents a company within the EscopoV3 system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Empresa entity.

cnpj.description: The CNPJ (Brazilian corporate tax ID) of the company.

Usuario.title: Usuario
Usuario.description: Represents a user of the EscopoV3 system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Usuario entity.

funcao.description: The user's role or job title within the company.

LancamentoFiscal.title: LancamentoFiscal
LancamentoFiscal.description: Represents a fiscal entry (nota fiscal) in the EscopoV3 system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the LancamentoFiscal entity.

tipo.description: The type of fiscal entry (e.g., venda, compra, servico).

dataEmissao.description: The date the fiscal document was issued.

valorTotal.description: The total value of the fiscal document.

Parceiro.title: Parceiro
Parceiro.description: Represents a business partner (customer, vendor, etc.) in the EscopoV3 system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Parceiro entity.

tipo.description: The type of partner (e.g., cliente, fornecedor).

documento.description: The partner's tax ID (CPF or CNPJ).

PlanoDeContas.title: PlanoDeContas
PlanoDeContas.description: Represents the chart of accounts in the EscopoV3 system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the PlanoDeContas entity.

natureza.description: The nature of the account (e.g., devedora, credora).

LancamentoContabil.title: LancamentoContabil
LancamentoContabil.description: Represents a journal entry in the EscopoV3 system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the LancamentoContabil entity.

data.description: The date of the journal entry.

descricao.description: The description of the journal entry.

debitoContaId.description: Reference to PlanoDeContas for debit account. (Relationship: PlanoDeContas 1:N LancamentoContabil)

creditoContaId.description: Reference to PlanoDeContas for credit account. (Relationship: PlanoDeContas 1:N LancamentoContabil)

valor.description: The amount of the journal entry.

Evento.title: Evento
Evento.description: Represents an event in the EscopoV3 system's calendar.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Evento entity.

dataInicio.description: The start date and time of the event.

dataFim.description: The end date and time of the event.

Arquivo.title: Arquivo
Arquivo.description: Represents a file stored within the EscopoV3 system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Arquivo entity.

url.description: The URL where the file is stored.

tipo.description: The MIME type of the file.

Funcionario.title: Funcionario
Funcionario.description: Represents an employee of a company within the EscopoV3 system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Funcionario entity.

nome.description: The full name of the employee.

cpf.description: The employee's CPF (Brazilian individual tax ID).

Rubrica.title: Rubrica
Rubrica.description: Represents a payroll code (rubrica) used in the EscopoV3 system for personnel calculations.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Rubrica entity.

descricao.description: A description of the payroll code.

tipo.description: The type of payroll code (e.g., provento, desconto).

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to adhere to the principles of Authorization Independence, Clarity of Intent, and Homogeneous Security Posture. It uses path-based ownership for user and company-related data and denormalizes authorization data where necessary to avoid `get()` calls in security rules. All collections are designed with a homogeneous security posture, ensuring that documents within a collection share the same security requirements.

*   **Authorization Independence:** Achieved by using path-based ownership (e.g., `/empresas/{empresaId}/usuarios/{usuarioId}`) and denormalizing authorization data into subcollections when needed. For example, if we had collaborative documents, the `members` map from the parent would be copied into the child documents.
*   **QAPs (Rules are not Filters):** Supported by segregating data with different access needs into different collections. For example, company data is separated by `empresaId`, enabling secure `list` operations within a company's scope. Private user data is stored under `/users/{userId}`, ensuring only the user can access it.
*   **DBAC:** Roles would be managed via a separate collection `/roles_admin/{uid}`. However, the current schema doesn't have this feature implemented.

The structure prioritizes clarity, security, and scalability, making it easier to implement robust security rules and maintain the application over time.
